# Follow-up on PR #767: make the hostId first-boot trap a step, not a troubleshooting entry

Your doc handles the hostId mismatch only under "Boot stops at cannot import 'wpool'". But with
`boot.zfs.forceImportRoot = false`, that failure is the DEFAULT outcome of the install as
written: disko creates and imports the pool under the installer's random hostid, nixos-install
does not export it, and the first boot of the installed system (hostid 74182f4c) then refuses
the import as a foreign pool. The owner is installing tonight; the step must be in the path.

Change `docs/weller-build-2026.md` install steps:

1. Before the disko step, add: set the installer's hostid to weller's committed value so the
   pool is created and last-imported under it —
   `zgenhostid -f 74182f4c` (zgenhostid ships with the zfs userland in the installer; verify
   the flag form against `zgenhostid --help` semantics: `zgenhostid [-f] [-o file] [hostid]`).
2. As a belt-and-braces final step before reboot: `umount -R /mnt && zpool export wpool`, with
   one sentence on why (a cleanly exported pool imports on any hostid; an un-exported one is
   "potentially active" and refused).
3. Keep the troubleshooting entry, but make it reference the two steps above as the thing that
   was skipped.

Also confirm `hosts/weller/disk-config.nix` / the disko zpool has no setting that would
contradict this (e.g. nothing forcing import). Push to the PR branch; paste `nix flake check`
final lines (docs-only change, but run it).
